answer: Shadow-grading divergence audit resists sybil graders: a hidden secondary panel of trusted graders independently scores a random hidden subset each voyage, and any primary grader whose scores systematically diverge from the shadow panel is flagged. A ring moving in lockstep on its own members produces an ocean of divergence from the honest shadow baseline that no genuine grader shows. The sable shadow panel is unpredictable and unseen, so a colluding cluster cannot know which of its grades are checked — systematic divergence strips its standing.
